pull_requests.title: Feature/ag UI copilot kit
pull_requests.author: TienNgen
pull_requests.body:
## Summary

Replaces the custom React chat UI with **CopilotKit** and connects it to the .NET
Orchestrator using the **AG-UI protocol**, including support for **frontend tools**
(LLM-invoked actions that execute in the browser).

## What's included

### New CopilotKit web client (`my-copilot-app`)
- Next.js 16 + CopilotKit v1.59 chat UI.
- Agent selector — agents are discovered from the Orchestrator (`/api/agents`) and switchable at runtime.
- Runs automatically with the rest of the stack via `dotnet run --project NTG.Agent.AppHost`.
- Thinking-mode badge in the agent selector.

### Native AG-UI endpoint in .NET (NTG.Agent.Orchestrator)
- New AgUiController (POST /api/agui/{agentId}) — the Orchestrator now natively emits AG-UI SSE events (RUN_STARTED, - TEXT_MESSAGE_*, TOOL_CALL_*, STEP_*, RUN_FINISHED/RUN_ERROR)
- New AgUiRunRequest DTOs matching the AG-UI RunAgentInput schema
- Thread→conversation mapping via ConcurrentDictionary<string, Guid> (no DB migration needed)

### Next.js is now a thin pass-through
- route.ts replaced custom NtgAgent with HttpAgent from @ag-ui/client — no custom translation code
- Deleted: _ntgAgent.ts, _bufferUtils.ts, _conversationStore.ts
- Session cookies are forwarded from the browser to the .NET backend via the HttpAgent headers

### Frontend tools (AG-UI flagship feature)
- PromptContentType.ToolCall chunk type and optional FrontendToolsJson field on AgUiRunRequest
- FrontendToolDeclaration (declaration-only AIFunctionDeclaration): tools are described to the LLM but executed in the browser; the model's call streams back as TOOL_CALL_* events
- Demo tool change_background: ask the agent to change the page background and it happens live, with a generative-UI status card in the chat
- Tools live in my-copilot-app/src/tools/ — add a component there to register a new tool
- video demo: 


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/751eb529-4387-47c2-ba01-18ec23504074


## How to test

1. dotnet run --project NTG.Agent.AppHost (requires SQL Server; starts backend + web client)
2. Open http://localhost:3000 and chat normally — responses stream as before.
3. Ask: "change the background color to "any color" " → the page background changes, a tool-call card appears in the chat, and the agent confirms the action.
4. In the Admin panel, set an agent's Mode to Thinking. The agent selector shows a "Thinking" badge for that agent.
5. Regression: the Blazor WebClient chat is unaffected.

commit_records.message:
LightRAG per-agent: attach containers to a stable shared network

Fixes upload failing with "connection reset"/"connection refused": spawned agent
containers were not actually attached to Aspire's network (NetworkMode alone is
unreliable), so LightRAG couldn't resolve lightrag-postgres (name-resolution failure,
crash loop) and Docker never applied the host port mapping (NetworkSettings.Ports empty).

  containers to it explicitly via NetworkingConfig.EndpointsConfig (not just NetworkMode).

  `lightrag-postgres` alias, so agents resolve it across AppHost restarts (Aspire's
  per-session network is ephemeral and would otherwise orphan persistent containers).

  any that are detached or have no live port mapping (auto-heals after restarts).

pull_requests.title: [AI-1] Fix Azure OpenAI v1 reasoning routing; extract two-axis provider client factories
pull_requests.author: AnVuGia
pull_requests.body:
## Summary

Fixes Azure OpenAI v1 endpoint routing for DeepSeek reasoning models, then extracts the inline per-provider client construction in `AgentFactory` into a two-axis client factory design:

- **Provider axis** — `IAgentClientFactory`, resolved via keyed DI on `ProviderName`:
  - `OpenAICompatibleClientFactory` (OpenAI, GitHubModel, GoogleGemini, AzureOpenAI)
  - `AnthropicClientFactory` (Anthropic)
- **Reasoning axis** — `ReasoningSurfaceResolver` picks the reasoning surface per model *and provider*: `None`, `ResponsesApi`, or `ChatCompletionsEffort`. DeepSeek models route to Chat Completions on every provider (the Responses API rejects `reasoning.effort` for them with HTTP 400 `unsupported_parameter`). GitHub Models and Google Gemini route to Chat Completions regardless of model, because neither platform exposes a `/responses` endpoint at all (verified by probe — see Verification).
- Shared middleware (FunctionInvocation, OpenTelemetry) is unified in `ChatClientPipeline.BuildStandard()`.

`AgentFactory` now resolves the right factory per provider instead of carrying ~200 lines of inline `CreateOpenAI/Anthropic/AzureOpenAIAgentAsync` + `CreateBasic*` variants.

### Key findings behind the routing (verified against official docs + live probes)

1. **Not every "OpenAI-compatible" provider has the Responses API.** GitHub Models (`models.github.ai/inference`) and Gemini's OpenAI-compat layer expose **no `/responses` endpoint** — probed live: both return 404 while control calls on `chat/completions` succeed with the same credentials. Thinking agents on these providers therefore *must* use Chat Completions `reasoning_effort` (documented by Gemini; undocumented but Azure-backed on GitHub Models).
2. **DeepSeek models reject Responses-API reasoning everywhere.** `reasoning.effort` → HTTP 400 `unsupported_parameter`; they take a top-level `reasoning_effort` on Chat Completions and return chain-of-thought as `reasoning_content` (verified live against Azure `/openai/v1`).
3. **The old code's thinking path never worked on GitHub Models / Gemini** — it sent Responses-API requests to `api.openai.com` with the wrong provider's key. This PR fixes both the address (respects `ProviderEndpoint`) and the surface (routes to Chat Completions).
4. **OpenAI reasoning-summary verbosity is per-model** and may require org verification, so the Responses path uses `summary: auto` (OpenAI's documented recommendation) rather than pinning `detailed`.

## Intentional behavior changes

These are deliberate unifications introduced by the refactor — flagging them so they aren't mistaken for regressions:

1. **Thinking-effort mapping**: OpenAI thinking effort `Medium`/`Full` now maps to `High`/`Auto` via `RawRepresentationFactory`. `Auto` (not `Detailed`) follows OpenAI's docs: summary-verbosity support varies per model and `auto` selects the best available; some verbosity levels also require organization verification.
2. **Endpoint fix**: GitHubModel/GoogleGemini *thinking* agents now respect the configured `ProviderEndpoint` — the old inline code silently hit `api.openai.com` (latent bug).
3. **DeepSeek routing scope**: the DeepSeek → Chat Completions routing now applies to *all* OpenAI-compatible providers, not just Azure OpenAI.
5. **GitHub Models / Gemini thinking surface**: thinking agents on these providers now use Chat Completions `reasoning_effort` instead of the Responses API. Neither platform has a `/responses` endpoint (GitHub's REST reference lists only `chat/completions`; Gemini's OpenAI-compat docs list chat completions/embeddings/images/video/batch), so the old Responses-API path could never have worked there — on either side of this refactor.
4. **Basic agent middleware**: the naming/summarization agent now gets the same FunctionInvocation + OpenTelemetry middleware as chat agents (previously had none).

## Design notes

Rationale kept out of code comments by choice — recorded here instead:

- **Azure via plain `OpenAIClient`**: Azure's `/openai/v1` surface accepts the standard client with the key as a Bearer token; `AzureOpenAIClient` only speaks the legacy api-version deployment API and cannot address `/openai/v1`. (Also noted in a short comment, since the registration otherwise looks like a bug.)
- **Anthropic gets its own factory** because it doesn't speak the OpenAI wire protocol and configures extended thinking via `MessageCreateParams` through `RawRepresentationFactory` — the only path the Microsoft.Extensions.AI adapter supports.
- **`ChatClientPipeline.BuildStandard()`** centralizes the `.UseFunctionInvocation().UseOpenTelemetry()` chain that was previously copy-pasted into every provider/mode branch; factories supply only the reasoning-specific `ChatOptions`.
- **DeepSeek's chain-of-thought** returns as `reasoning_content`, which Microsoft.Extensions.AI maps to the same `TextReasoningContent` type the Responses path emits — so the streaming/UI layer needs no changes.
- **`CreateBasicAgent` passes `enableThinking: false`** so the naming/summarization agent never incurs reasoning cost regardless of the default agent's configured mode.
- **Anthropic thinking budget**: `ThinkingTokens` must be ≥1024 and below `MaxTokens` (API constraint).

## Verification

- 243/243 orchestrator unit tests pass, 0 skipped.
- Falsified at the real API surface against the Azure `/openai/v1` endpoint (DeepSeek-V4-Pro):
  - Chat Completions + top-level `reasoning_effort: high` → HTTP 200 with `reasoning_content` populated.
  - Responses API `reasoning.effort` for DeepSeek → HTTP 400 `unsupported_parameter` (why we route away).
  - gpt-5.1 on Responses API → 200 (non-DeepSeek branch unaffected).
- Routing is deterministic (model-name + provider-name match) and covered by dedicated `ReasoningSurfaceResolverTests` (249 total tests green).
- Endpoint-existence probes (2026-07-22): GitHub Models `POST /inference/responses` → **404** with a 200 control on `chat/completions` using the same token; Gemini `POST /v1beta/openai/responses` → **404** while the same (invalid) key gets a 400 auth error on the real `chat/completions` route — proving the 404 is the route, not auth.
- Caveat: `reasoning_effort` acceptance on GitHub-hosted *reasoning* models could not be runtime-verified — every reasoning model on the test token's tier is unavailable (400/403/500 before the parameter is even evaluated). A non-reasoning model rejects the parameter with Azure-style `Unrecognized request argument`, consistent with per-model validation. Gemini documents `reasoning_effort: high` officially.

Also includes: `.gitignore` entries for local `.env` / `.env.example` files.

pull_requests.author: AnVuGia
pull_requests.body:
## One-command local install: `install.sh` bootstrap + self-installing `install-local.sh`

Builds on #282 (stacked; merge after it). Follow-up promised in #283 ("paves the way for one-command install scripts").

```
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nashtech-garage/ntg-agent/main/install.sh | bash
```

On a fresh Ubuntu box that line ends at a running AppHost with a chat-ready Default Agent — no Admin UI configuration, no manual prerequisite setup. Windows is supported via WSL2 (same line inside the WSL shell; Docker Desktop owns Docker there).

### What it does

| Phase | `install-local.sh` |
|---|---|
| 1 Prereqs | Checks .NET 10 SDK, Docker CLI + daemon access + compose, Node ≥ 20, git/curl/openssl. **On Ubuntu/Debian it `sudo apt`-installs whatever is missing** (`dotnet-sdk-10.0`, `docker.io docker-compose-v2` + enable daemon + add user to `docker` group, Node 22 LTS from NodeSource, git/curl/openssl), then re-execs itself through `sg docker -c` so the new group applies without a re-login and re-runs the checks. A guard env var stops the loop if apt couldn't fix something (hints + exit 1). Non-apt systems (Arch, macOS) and Docker-on-WSL keep the hints-and-exit path. |
| 2 Repo tooling | Activates `.githooks`, installs `dotnet-ef` (and puts `~/.dotnet/tools` on PATH — fresh shells don't have it), ensures the HTTPS dev cert. |
| 3 `.env` | Creates from `.env.example`; prompts only for `LIGHTRAG_AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT` + `LIGHTRAG_EMBEDDING_API_KEY` (your own Azure OpenAI resource; deployment names default to `gpt-5.1` / `text-embedding-3-large`, overridable in `.env`); generates `SA_PASSWORD`, `LIGHTRAG_PG_PASSWORD`, `LIGHTRAG_API_KEY`. Re-runs keep existing values. |
| 4 User-secrets | Runs `scripts/init-apphost-user-secrets.sh` non-interactively (now also writes `sql-sa-password`). |
| 5 LightRAG | `docker compose up -d` in `deploy/lightrag-local`, waits on Postgres + gateway health. |
| 6 Launch | execs `start-local-lightrag.sh` (AppHost). |

`install.sh` (new, top-level) is the from-nothing entry: installs git via apt if missing, clones (`NTG_BRANCH` / `NTG_DIR` / `NTG_REPO_URL` overridable), reattaches `/dev/tty` as stdin so the secret prompts survive the pipe, execs `install-local.sh`.

**`DefaultAgentProviderSeeder`** (run-once hosted service in the Orchestrator) backfills the seeded Default Agent's empty provider with **Azure OpenAI** (endpoint/key/chat deployment reused from `LightRag:Llm*`, endpoint suffixed `/openai/v1` for the chat factory). Admin edits are never overwritten. GitHub Models was the first choice but is being retired (observed `410 github_models_retirement_brownout` on 2026-08-12), which would permanently break every fresh install post-retirement.

### Verification

- Unit: `DefaultAgentProviderSeederTests` (4 tests: fills when empty, leaves configured provider, ignores non-default agents, no-ops on incomplete Azure config). Full Orchestrator suite green.
- **Pristine Ubuntu 24.04 VM (QEMU, disk reset from the untouched cloud image):**
  - 2026-08-12 (check-only Phase 1, prereqs pre-installed by hand): unattended install → seeder fired → login → first chat answered with reasoning trace + auto-naming, zero Admin UI touches. Found and fixed the `~/.dotnet/tools` PATH gap.
  - 2026-08-19 (this auto-install Phase 1, via the bootstrap): 5 prereqs missing → installed (dotnet 10.0.111, node 22.23, docker 29.1 + compose 2.40) → `sg` re-exec → checks green → Phase 2 → stopped at the secret prompt (headless run, no TTY — by design). Docker group access persists in a fresh shell.
  - 2026-08-20 (`cc9cb6d`, interactive over `ssh -t` on the same VM): endpoint + key prompts → LightRAG stack healthy → AppHost up → webclient login → first chat answered (user-verified). Dashboard/webclient reached from the host through an SSH port forward.
- Host stub tests of the apt path (command sequence, re-exec, loop guard) and the non-apt path.

### Also removed: the dead `github-token` parameter (`d953174`)

Nothing reads `GitHub:Models:GitHubToken` — the GitHub Models provider takes its key from the per-agent `ApiKey` in the DB, and the seeder moved to Azure. It survived only because Aspire blocks startup on an unresolved parameter. Dropped end-to-end: AppHost parameter + env, `init-apphost-user-secrets.sh` field/required-check/write, `.env.example` key, orphaned `GitHub:Models` blocks in both Orchestrator `appsettings*.json`, README PAT step, installer prompt. Existing dev machines are unaffected (an unused user-secret is ignored). Verified: AppHost builds; secrets-script `--dry-run` no longer lists it; headless VM re-run on `d953174` stops at the Azure-key prompt only.

### Also fixed: the hard-coded Azure resource (`cc9cb6d`)

Since #265 the AppHost hard-coded one developer's resource (`rmit-capstone-2026-hcm--resource.openai.azure.com`) and the deployment names `gpt-5.1` / `text-embedding-3-large` as LightRAG's LLM + embedding endpoints; the seeder inherited it, so a newcomer's own key would be sent to the wrong resource. Now three Aspire parameters — `lightrag-azure-openai-endpoint`, `lightrag-llm-model`, `lightrag-embedding-model` — fed from `.env` by the secrets script (endpoint required, models default). **Existing checkouts: re-run `./scripts/init-apphost-user-secrets.sh` once** (or set the three user-secrets by hand; Aspire holds startup on an unresolved parameter). Verified: AppHost builds, seeder tests green, secrets `--dry-run` requires the endpoint and defaults the models, headless VM run stops at the endpoint prompt.

### Known / deliberately not done

- Pre-existing: Admin UI "test connection" for Azure appends `/openai/deployments` to the stored endpoint, which conflicts with the `/openai/v1` base the chat factory uses.
- The bootstrap's install-git branch wasn't exercised on the VM (the Ubuntu cloud image ships git).
- NodeSource's setup script is a remote script piped to `sudo bash` (major-version pinned, `setup_22.x`); apt's `nodejs` on noble is 18 and Next.js 16 needs ≥ 20.9.

pull_requests.title: feat: Agent Skills,  validated A2UI surface templates bound per agent
pull_requests.author: TienNgen
pull_requests.body:
## Agent Skills, and the A2UI path they render through

Adds **Agent Skills** to the orchestrator: an admin uploads a ZIP containing a `SKILL.md` and
pre-authored A2UI surface templates, binds it to an agent, and the model drives a multi-step
interactive flow in the chat — collecting input, offering options, taking a confirmation — using
surfaces a human designed rather than ones the model invents each turn.

Two demo packages ship with it: `travel-planning` (a three-step tabbed wizard) and
`ticket-booking` (three separate cards). Both fabricate all data and neither claims a booking.

Also carries the fixes and hardening found while building it, listed below.

`origin/main` is an ancestor of this branch, so **this fast-forwards with no conflicts.**

---

### Why this exists

The repo already had generative UI, but it was per-tool hardcoded React —
`WeatherCardTool.tsx` matches `get_weather` by name and renders a bespoke card. Every new
visual answer needed a new component and a deploy.

A2UI replaced the hardcoding with a declarative catalog the model composes against
(**Path A**, `render_a2ui`). That generalises but drifts: the model re-authors the layout every
turn, and nothing validates it. Skills close that gap (**Path B**, `render_skill_surface`) — the
tree is authored once by a person and validated at import; only the data changes at run time.

Both paths ship. The weather card still works, unchanged.

---

### What a reviewer needs to do

**Run the migration.** `20260809163504_AddAgentSkills` adds three tables: `Skills`,
`SkillAssets`, `AgentSkills`.

> If you have a local DB that saw an earlier `AddAgentSkills` from a different branch, you will
> hit `Error 2714` on an object that already exists. Drop the stale `AgentSkills` table and its
> `__EFMigrationsHistory` row in one transaction, then migrate.

**Nothing else is required.** Bundled packages seed themselves on startup from `seed/skills/`
(override with `Skills:SeedDirectory`). Two Next.js switches exist and both default to on:
`A2UI_STABLE_SURFACE_IDS` and `A2UI_FREEFORM_TOOL`.

---

### The shape of it

**Three-tier progressive disclosure.** A bound skill's name and description go into the system
prompt on every run (cheap). `load_skill` returns the body only when the model decides it is
relevant. `render_skill_surface` reads a template from `assets/`, merges the model's `values`
into its data model, and emits `createSurface` / `updateComponents` / `updateDataModel` — so the
model supplies content, never layout.

**Validated at import, not on screen.** `SurfaceValidator` checks every template against
`A2uiCatalog.cs` and returns *all* failures at once. The check that matters most is the seed
rule: A2UI inputs are controlled components whose setter is a no-op until the bound path exists,
so an unseeded field renders, accepts focus, and silently refuses typing — with no error in the
console, the logs, or the SSE stream. That is now a rejected upload instead.

**Admin-only API** at `api/skills`: import, list, inspect, export, delete, and bind/unbind per
agent. Plus a Skills page and an import modal in the Blazor admin.

---

### Security

A `SKILL.md` is instructions injected straight into an LLM's context, so an uploaded package is
untrusted input with an unusually direct path to the model. The threat model and full control
matrices are in [`docs/skill-import-security.md`](docs/skill-import-security.md). The parts
worth knowing before reviewing:

- **Path validation runs on the raw `FullName` string, never through `Path.*`.** On Linux `\` is
  an ordinary filename character, so `..\..\evil.md` normalises to an inert single-component
  name and a `Path.GetFullPath` check reports no escape — while the same string is real
  traversal on Windows. CI is Linux, so that check would have passed while being wrong.
- **Validate and store the same value.** `ZipArchive.GetEntry` returns the *first* match while
  EF upsert iteration keeps the *last*, so validating one way and storing the other means the
  reviewed content is not the stored content. That defeats human review of the exact bytes that
  become instructions, and it is the sharpest attack available here.
- **Invisible characters are rejected**, including the `U+E0000–U+E007F` tag block, bidi
  overrides, and `U+0085` / `U+2028` / `U+2029` — which cleared both the control-character check
  and the zero-width check while still being line breaks to every tokenizer.
- **`scripts/` is deliberately not supported**, which removes the RCE class outright and is doing
  more work than every other control combined.

Content-level prompt injection is bounded, not defended. That is accepted for admin-only import
and is stated in the doc.

---

### Fixes carried along

| Fix | Symptom it removes |
|---|---|
| Responses API held stateless | `previous_response_id` chaining made Azure return HTTP 400 `previous_response_not_found` after a successful tool call, killing the run. Measured 4 of 6 runs failing before, 6 of 6 passing after |
| Generative UI gated on client capability | The Blazor chat pasted raw protocol JSON into the assistant's bubble; `FrontendToolsJson` and `PersistUserMessage` were also caller-supplied on a `[FromForm]` endpoint |
| AG-UI access denial answered as a message | An inaccessible agent produced `INTERNAL_ERROR` in the browser, and created an orphan conversation row per attempt |
| `Tabs` child references resolved in validation | Tabs was unusable in a package — valid surfaces rejected, dangling refs unreported |
| Kind-preserving `values` merge | A wrong-shaped value could overwrite a seeded object and freeze every input beneath it |
| Stable surface ids | A re-rendered surface opened a second card, stranding the user's answers in the first |
| Label/value rows | A price broke across two lines as "$42" / "0" |
| SQL Server pinned to `2025-latest` | The 2022 image crash-loops on WSL2 6.6.x kernels |

---

### Testing

**600 tests pass, 0 fail** (585 orchestrator + 15 MCP server). **282 are new**, the largest
groups being `SurfaceValidatorTests` (70), `SkillPackageImporterTests` (57) and
`SurfaceRenderFunctionTests` (47).

`dotnet build` and `npm run build` both clean.

Three scripts back the parts unit tests cannot reach: `scripts/check-skill-flow.py` drives the
full three-turn travel flow against a running app, `scripts/check-a2ui-guide.py` guards the
render guide's prop names against the real schema, and `scripts/pack-skills.py` builds the
packages. `A2uiCatalogDriftTests` re-derives the C# catalog snapshot from
`basic_catalog.json` when present, so an npm bump fails a test rather than causing a mystery
import rejection.

**Manual check, if you want one:** import `seed/skills/travel-planning.zip` via Admin → Skills,
bind it to an agent, then in `my-copilot-app` ask *"Help me plan a trip to Da Nang in
September"*. The card should render with the destination pre-filled, then move through Options
and Review **in place** — one card, not three.

---

### Docs

| Document | Covers |
|---|---|
| [`docs/README.md`](docs/README.md) | Index and reading order |
| [`docs/A2UI-and-AG-UI.md`](docs/A2UI-and-AG-UI.md) | How a surface reaches the screen; Path A vs Path B; decisions, corrections, open gaps |
| [`docs/Writing-a-SKILL.md`](docs/Writing-a-SKILL.md) | Authoring, packing and testing a skill |
| [`docs/AGUI-Surface-Template-Design.md`](docs/AGUI-Surface-Template-Design.md) | Designing a template: anatomy, naming, data-model contract, three archetypes |
| [`docs/skill-import-security.md`](docs/skill-import-security.md) | Importer threat model and controls |

Also corrects two pre-existing docs: `monitoring-setup.md` described an `IApplicationLogger<T>`
and a `LoggingMiddleware` that do not exist, and `agents-as-tools-architecture.md` predated the
Access tab, the Skills sub-tab and four `agentadmin` endpoints. The two implementation plans are
retired, their durable content folded into the reference docs above.

---

### Known limitations

- **Freeform `render_a2ui` surfaces are not replayed on page reload.** Skill surfaces are.
- **`render_a2ui` is still declared on every run of every agent**, so its ~130-line guide is
  prepended even when a bound skill owns the surface. `A2UI_FREEFORM_TOOL` turns it off
  per deployment; a per-agent switch is open work.
- **Skill tests all use `UseInMemoryDatabase`.** `GetActiveSkillAssetAsync`'s SQL Server
  translation is unproven.
- **No skill versioning.** Re-import overwrites in place, keeping the row so bindings survive. A
  SHA-256 of each imported body is logged for traceability, but the UI does not yet confirm a
  replacement.
- **The label/value CSS fix is verified by build and an isolated repro only** — not yet
  confirmed in the running app.
- Demo skills fabricate all data by design.

commit_records.author: TienNgen
commit_records.message:
feat(skills): add A2UI surface validator

Validates the hand-authored surface templates a skill bundles under
assets/, so a malformed template is a rejected upload with a line-item
error list rather than a blank card mid-demo.

A2uiCatalog is a flattened snapshot of the v0.9 basic catalog: the schema
composes each component from ComponentCommon, CatalogComponentCommon and
Checkable via allOf, so those properties are folded into each entry. It
is a snapshot because the schema lives in the frontend's node_modules,
which the Orchestrator cannot reach.

SurfaceValidator checks component names, required and unknown
properties, enum values, child reference resolution, self-references,
orphans, and the root being a layout component. The subtle check is the
last one: every {path} binding must have a seed in `data`, because an
unseeded path renders the input frozen — A2UI inputs are controlled
components whose setter is a no-op until the path exists.

Returns all failures rather than the first; an author fixing one error
per upload round-trip starts disabling checks.

commit_records.author: TienNgen
commit_records.message:
fix(skills): resolve Tabs child references in surface validation
Tabs.tabs is an array of { title, child } objects, so its child reference
sits one level below every other component's. The traversal only looked
at top-level reference properties, which was wrong in both directions: a
valid Tabs surface was rejected with every pane reported as an orphan
that "will not render", while a genuinely dangling child produced no
error at all. Tabs was unusable in a skill package.

Also validate shadowed duplicate components. IndexComponents keeps the
first definition, so a duplicated id left the second copy's own defects
unreported — the author fixes the id, re-uploads, and gets a fresh round
of errors, which is the round-trip the report-everything design exists to
avoid. Emitted errors are now de-duplicated so this costs no noise.

Adds SurfaceValidatorTests (69 cases) covering document structure,
component properties, child references, data bindings and error
accumulation, with one case per dead property name from the old render
guide as a regression anchor.

Adds A2uiCatalogDriftTests, which re-derives the catalog from
basic_catalog.json — resolving the allOf/$ref composition that supplies
id, accessibility, weight and checks — and fails on divergence, so
bumping the npm package surfaces here rather than as a mystery import
rejection later.

Icon.name is deliberately left without an enum. Its oneOf has three
branches — the 59-name enum, a bare { type: string }, and a { path }
binding — so any string is schema-valid and enforcing the enum would
reject legitimate surfaces.

commit_records.author: TienNgen
commit_records.message:
feat(skills): make bound skills usable at run time

Three-tier progressive disclosure per the Agent Skills spec. Tier 1 is a
catalog of names and descriptions; tier 2 is load_skill returning the
SKILL.md body on demand; tier 3 is render_skill_surface, which draws a
stored A2UI template.

render_skill_surface is deliberately not built on CapturingAIFunction,
which returns its result to the model unchanged — that would dump the
whole surface JSON back into context on every render. The browser gets
the full operations through RenderableToolCapture; the model gets a
one-line receipt.

Both tools close over the agent id rather than taking it as a parameter,
and every lookup re-checks the skill is bound and enabled for that agent,
so a model naming another agent's skill gets nothing.

Sanitize now asks Unicode what a character is rather than matching a list
of known offenders. U+0085, U+2028 and U+2029 are all above 0x20, so they
clear the control-character check while renderers and tokenizers still
treat them as line breaks — a description carrying one could break out of
its catalog entry.

commit_records.author: TienNgen
commit_records.message:
feat(skills): seed bundled skill packages on startup

Imports seed/skills/*.zip through the same importer and registry an admin
upload uses, so a fresh clone demos without manual setup and the import
path is exercised on every cold start rather than only when someone clicks
Import.

It never replaces. ImportAsync updates a same-named skill in place, so
re-seeding every start would silently discard an admin's edits and reset
their assets. Identity is the name frontmatter rather than the file name,
read by running the importer's own parse — which writes nothing, since the
caller owns the transaction — so the seeder cannot disagree with the
importer about what a package is called.

Seeded skills record ImportedByUserId = Guid.Empty. Attributing
instructions to an admin who never saw them would defeat the column's
purpose, and Identity never mints an empty GUID, so the marker cannot
collide with a real importer. Skills are not bound to any agent; binding
stays an explicit admin decision.

Contained so it can never prevent startup, and a scope per package rather
than per run: after a failed SaveChangesAsync EF still tracks the rejected
entity, which a shared context would replay into every later package.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit_records.author: TienNgen
commit_records.message:
feat(a2ui): let a re-rendered surface update its card in place

Three pieces that together turn a stacking wizard into one card.

StableSurfaceIdMiddleware rewrites the activity messageId from
a2ui-surface-<surfaceId>-<callId> to a stable a2ui-surface-<surfaceId>.
CopilotKit keys activity messages by id, so the suffix was what forced a
new React element, a new A2UIProvider and a new empty store on every
render. With it removed, @ag-ui/client replaces the message at its index
and the same surface updates in place.

Scoped to render_skill_surface only, by tracking callId to tool name from
the TOOL_CALL_START events already on the stream. A skill authors its
surfaceId and A2UI treats that as the surface's identity, so collapsing is
protocol-correct; freeform render_a2ui ids are model-invented per turn and
reused across unrelated asks, where collapsing would silently rewrite a
card further up the transcript. Gated by A2UI_STABLE_SURFACE_IDS, matching
the existing A2UI_FREEFORM_TOOL idiom. The surfaceId is read from the
operations rather than split off the id, because surfaceIds contain dashes.

InteractiveTabs makes Tabs steerable. The stock component holds its
selected index in local React state with no binding and no action, so the
agent could neither read nor set it, and TabsApi is strict — a declared
prop would mean forking the schema. Instead it reads /__tabs/<componentId>
from the data model, the symmetric read half of the /__inputs convention
the other overrides already write. A change to that path moves the user; a
repeat of the value already delivered does not, so a user who navigates
away is not dragged back on the next render. It mirrors {index, title}
back, because a bare index tells a model reading formData nothing.

SkillSurfaceTool's stand-down check keyed on the toolCallId appearing in
the messageId, which the rewrite removes, so it would have painted a
second copy alongside the live one. Re-keyed on surfaceId, still matching
the old id shape for conversations persisted before this change. Restore
now paints only the newest render per surface, which live and reloaded
views previously disagreed about.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit_records.author: TienNgen
commit_records.message:
feat(skills): render travel-planning as one tabbed surface

The three-step flow now lives in a single surface, trip-planner
(surfaceId trip-wizard), whose root Column holds a Tabs component. The
agent advances the user by seeding /__tabs/wizard, so submitting a step
moves the tab instead of appending another card. Earlier tabs stay open,
which is what makes reviewing an earlier answer possible without scrolling
back through the transcript.

Two changes to the render function make that safe.

Values that would change a seeded path's kind are refused rather than
merged. The template's data block is the schema, and prose in SKILL.md was
the only thing describing the shape — so {"trip": "Da Nang"}, well-formed
JSON and a plausible thing for a model to send, replaced the seeded /trip
object and left every input under it frozen. That is the unseeded-path
failure the surface validator exists to prevent, recreated at run time past
the point validation reaches. The refusal names the path and lists the
expected keys so the model can correct itself.

The data model is written one top-level branch at a time, never at the
root. A root write replaces everything, including the /__inputs mirrors
that carry the user's own typed answers back to the agent — harmless while
each render made a fresh card, and silent data loss the moment a surface is
rendered twice. Branch writes are free on a first render, where the model
is empty and each key is created exactly as a root write would have.

Every branch is still emitted on every render, so a binding can never go
unseeded. The cost is that a branch the model omits is rewritten with its
placeholders, so SKILL.md instructs it to re-send options alongside review.
Emitting only supplied branches would preserve the rest but leave a first
render's unsupplied branches unseeded, which is a frozen input: silent,
where a reappearing placeholder is visible.

check-skill-flow.py now expects one surface across all three turns,
reassembles the data model from the per-branch writes, and asserts the
wizard advances 0 → 1 → 2 — without which the flow could render a single
card that never leaves step one and still pass every other check.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit_records.author: TienNgen
commit_records.message:
feat(skills): move the wizard on click, not on the agent's reply

A step button in a tabbed flow reads as "next", not "submit". Waiting for
the round trip left the user sitting on a form they had finished with for
ten to twenty seconds, with no sign the click had registered.

The button now advances the tab locally and sends the submission as
before; the agent's own /__tabs write lands on the tab we already moved to
and is a no-op. A template marks a button with "advanceTab": "<tabs id>"
in its action context, which is free-form, so this needed no schema
change. That key is stripped from the payload rather than sent to the
agent as though it were an answer. Confirm and Change deliberately do not
advance.

The tabs a user now lands on before the answer arrives are seeded with
copy that reads as progress rather than as an empty result.

Also strengthens the pre-fill instruction. It read "anything they already
told you pre-filled", which the model ignored — asking for a trip to Da Lat
rendered an empty destination field, so the user had to type it again. It
now names that case directly and says why it matters.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit_records.author: TienNgen
commit_records.message:
fix(a2ui): correct a stale Button variant, and teach layout in the guide

The guide contradicted itself: its prose told the model to give secondary
actions variant "secondary" or "text" while its own component table listed
default|primary|borderless. Those two names were removed from the catalog
in the Phase 0 correction and the prose was missed, because the regression
check only matched the pipe-separated spelling. It now matches the variant
names wherever they are named as variants.

The design section previously described tone and copy but almost nothing
about structure, which is the only thing the model actually controls —
colour, spacing and fonts belong to the host stylesheet. It now says so,
and names the three levers that do the work: Text variant, Row/Column
justify/align, and Divider.

The addition that matters most is the spaceBetween Row — label left, value
right, repeated down a Column. That is what makes a summary or a price
list read as a table rather than a paragraph, and nothing mentioned it. It
comes with a worked example, because the guide's own advice is that models
copy examples over prose.

`weight` is deliberately still absent. It is on every component in the
schema and the renderer ignores it entirely, so recommending it would be
recommending a no-op.

commit_records.author: TienNgen
commit_records.message:
feat(a2ui): give generated surfaces colour that holds in both themes

Adds a companion teal alongside the iris accent, tints field labels toward
that accent, and washes the card's top corner so it has a light source
rather than a flat fill. Colour now lands in three places — labels, the
active tab, the primary button — against a wide neutral field. The card
sits inside a chat transcript and must not shout over the conversation, so
everything else stays single-hue.

Every value is a token defined in both theme blocks. Dark needs more than
a palette swap: white on the dark accent is only 3.50:1, so the button
label flips to ink, and the corner wash goes to 8% because 5% moves a dark
ground by less than the eye registers.

Fixes several rules that never matched what they were aimed at:

- Sliders and radios were left at the browser default, so a pink track sat
  beside an iris button. Both now take accent-color.
- The Divider rule targeted <hr>; the catalog renders a <div> with a
  hardcoded #ccc. Keyed on that colour instead — but per PROPERTY, because
  the colour alone also matches the tab strip's border-bottom and the
  Card's border, and would have painted the divider's gradient across the
  whole background of both.
- The primary-button selector carried two rgb() spellings that can never
  appear: var() survives into the style attribute unresolved, so only the
  var() form matches. Tightened to the property so the active tab, which
  spends the same var on color and border-bottom, is left alone.
- label unqualified also caught every radio and checkbox row, turning a
  six-option list into six lines of indigo. Scoped so answers stay ink.
- Stock Card and Modal hardcode #fff, punching a white hole in a dark
  card; unchecked radios rendered as white discs without color-scheme.

The corner wash is written as a plain alpha rather than color-mix().
Lightning CSS cannot fold a color-mix() whose argument is a var(), and
shipped it as the accent at full opacity outside any @supports guard — a
solid indigo blob on browsers without color-mix.

Contrast measured against the washed corner rather than the flat card:
labels 6.48/8.32, captions 4.58/6.11, button text 4.75/5.17 (light/dark).
Input borders remain at 1.23:1, below WCAG 1.4.11's 3:1 for control
boundaries; raising them would visibly harden the card and is left as a
deliberate open question.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit_records.author: TienNgen
commit_records.message:
feat(chat): gate generative UI on what the client can render

A2UI surfaces, skill tools and tool-render cards only work in my-copilot-app. The Blazor web chat renders markdown and nothing else, and its stream loop appends every unrecognised chunk straight into the assistant's bubble — so anything sent there arrives as raw protocol JSON in the reply.

Detection is by endpoint, not by sniffing: the two clients already arrive at two different controllers, so each one states which it is. ChatClientCapabilities is a parameter rather than a property on PromptRequestForm because that type is [FromForm]-bound on the text-only endpoint — a capability declared there would be one any caller could grant itself. TextOnly is the zero value so a call site that forgets degrades to withholding rather than leaking.

Six gates: renderable tool calls, skill notices, the skill tier stack, FrontendToolsJson, and PersistUserMessage. The last two are the security-relevant ones. A crafted form post naming render_a2ui would otherwise pull the entire A2UI render guide into a run whose client cannot draw a surface; and PersistUserMessage is honoured only for the client that has tool-result follow-up turns, since on the other endpoint a crafted post would run the agent, spend the tokens, keep the reply, and quietly drop the user's own message from the transcript.

Skills go as a unit rather than trimmed to load_skill, because leaving that on alone hands the model a step-by-step flow whose every step names a tool it was not given.

DrainRenderableToolCalls and DrainSkillNotices split into a non-iterator wrapper plus an iterator: in the withholding branch, emptying the buffer is the method's only effect, and an effect that happens only if the caller enumerates the result is one a refactor can drop without a warning. Hence DiscardPending on both buffers.

One consequence worth stating: withholding the tool chunks also stops the Tool-role row being written, since the persisted envelope is built from those chunks. That is intended — the row exists so an A2UI client can rehydrate a card on reload — but a text-only conversation now stores no record of the call.

Chat.razor gets the second lock on the same door: it skips ToolCall and ToolResult outright, and routes SkillNotice into the thinking buffer. It locks those values only; PromptContentType is open and the else-branch is the default, so whoever adds a member has to come back.

Addresses the Copilot review on #286.

SkillPrompt.Sanitize flattened only Control, LineSeparator and
ParagraphSeparator, and iterated chars. Unicode tag characters
(U+E0000-U+E007F) are category Format and supplementary-plane, so a per-char
loop saw two Surrogates and matched neither -- but Format was missing from the
switch entirely, so BMP characters like U+200B ZERO WIDTH SPACE needed no
surrogates to slip through. Now iterates runes and flattens Format too.
SkillContentGuard already rejects these at import, so this is the
defence-in-depth path for skills stored before that check existed.

ToolManagementTab rendered skillsStatusMessage in a success alert whatever its
severity, so "Could not save skills" arrived green with a tick and read as if
it had worked. Now follows the isConnected pattern already used above it.

InteractiveTabs set aria-controls on every tab while rendering only the active
panel, leaving inactive tabs referencing elements not in the DOM.

BuildManifest's doc claimed values are written quoted; only metadata.version
is. The behaviour is safe -- the importer rejects newlines and structural
markers, so no value can break out of its line -- so the comment was corrected
rather than the emitter.

## Summary

Admins now curate which models are available per provider, with per-model
thinking-mode control. Agent settings surface only the enabled models and
gate Thinking mode on the provider's setting.

## Changes

**Provider settings (Providers page)**
- `Fetch Models` pulls the provider's catalog; admins enable models and
  toggle thinking per model. Thinking toggle is greyed out for models
  outside the backend's thinking-capable catalog.
- Azure OpenAI uses the AI Foundry **deployments** endpoint
  (`{account}.services.ai.azure.com/api/projects/{project}/deployments`),
  chat-completion deployments only; new Account/Project fields.
- New **Custom** provider type: no fetch; admins add models manually
  (OpenAI-compatible at runtime).
- `DefaultModel` removed from providers — agents now require an explicit
  model (existing data backfilled by the migration).

**Agent settings**
- Model dropdown shows only the provider's enabled models; Thinking mode
  enabled only when the admin allowed it for the selected model.

**Backend**
- `ProviderModel` entity + migration; `UpdateProvider` replaces the enabled
  list (fixes a `DbUpdateConcurrencyException` from client-generated keys).
- Thinking path honors custom endpoints (DeepSeek Responses API) and
  recognizes `deepseek-v4-*` as thinking-capable.
- LightRAG manager self-heals the shared Postgres container when it
  exists but is stopped (fixes chat hanging after thinking when the
  knowledge tool's backend was down).

**Verification**
- Full solution builds; 307/307 tests pass.
- Provider save/replace flows verified against the dev DB; Azure
  deployments fetch returns the 4 chat models; DeepSeek Responses API
  streams reasoning + final answer.

  models in the backend's thinking-capable catalog and is persisted
  per model

  manually (OpenAI-compatible at runtime)
- Azure OpenAI discovery uses the AI Foundry deployments endpoint
  (chat-completion deployments only); tolerant snake_case parsing
- Removed provider DefaultModel; agents require an explicit model
  (data backfilled in the migration)
- Fix UpdateProvider DbUpdateConcurrencyException when replacing
  enabled models (client-generated keys must be attached as Added)
- Thinking path honors custom endpoints (DeepSeek Responses API) and
  recognizes deepseek-v4 models as thinking-capable
- LightRag manager self-heals the shared Postgres container when it
  exists but is stopped

commit_records.message:
fix: route Azure OpenAI agents through the GA v1 inference surface

AzureOpenAIClient appends legacy routes (/openai/deployments/... with a
pinned preview api-version) onto the configured endpoint, so providers
whose endpoint already points at /openai/v1 (Foundry Target URI format)
404 on chat completions while responses-based thinking mode happens to
resolve. Build both agent modes and the basic agent on a plain
OpenAIClient against the normalized v1 base instead:
- fast mode -> POST /openai/v1/chat/completions (deployment name in model)
- thinking  -> POST /openai/v1/responses (unchanged reasoning config)
